review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–70) and checked its simp interface. The only simp-tagged declaration is `Fintype.sum_single_smul`. Its left side is `∑ i, Pi.single i₀ r i • f i` and its right side is `r • f i₀`. The rewrite shrinks the term, so it cannot cycle, and it is stated in the natural direction. I found no competing simp rule. The related `Finset.sum_pi_single` and `Finset.sum_pi_single'` are simp, but they cover sums without a smul. `Pi.single_apply` is not simp. The `Pi.single_smul` lemmas in `Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Action/Pi.lean` concern `single i (r • x)`, a different shape. `Finset.sum_smul`, `List.sum_smul` and `Multiset.sum_smul` are deliberately not simp; I found no `attribute [simp]` for them in Mathlib. Making them simp would expand sums and fight `smul_sum`. `Finset.cast_card` rewrites a cardinality into a sum, which is the wrong direction for simp. The sum form would simplify back to `#s`, so leaving it unannotated is right. `Finset.sum_smul_sum` and `Fintype.sum_smul_sum` expand a product of sums into a double sum, so they are also correctly not simp. I did not run Lean, so I have not tested whether `Fintype.sum_single_smul` fires on every intended instance. I did not search for a duplicate in other files beyond the greps above.
